questions.q: State what is meant by colour depth.

markPoints.concept: the number of bits used to store each pixel
markPoints.exemplar: The number of bits used for each pixel.

questions.example: The number of bits used to store the colour of each pixel.
questions.paraphrase: How many bits each individual pixel is given.
questions.feedback: Per pixel is the part that matters; it is what separates colour depth from resolution.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 13 — Pixel studio, station 2: Colour depth

questions.q: An image has a colour depth of 4 bits. How many different colours can each pixel be?
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 13 — Pixel studio, station 2: Colour depth

questions.q: Explain the difference between the resolution and the colour depth of an image.

markPoints.concept: resolution is the number of pixels in the image
markPoints.exemplar: Resolution is the number of pixels in the image.

markPoints.concept: colour depth is the number of bits used for each pixel
markPoints.exemplar: Colour depth is the number of bits used for each pixel.

questions.example: Resolution is how many pixels the image is made of, usually given as a width and a height. Colour depth is how many bits are used to store each one of those pixels.
questions.paraphrase: Resolution is the count of pixels in the picture, while colour depth is how many bits each pixel takes up.
questions.feedback: Both halves. One is a count of pixels, the other is bits per pixel.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 13 — Pixel studio, station 2: Colour depth

questions.q: State what is meant by metadata in an image file.

markPoints.concept: data about the image itself, rather than the pixels
accept: about the image|about the file|data about|information about|describes the|extra information|not the pixels
markPoints.exemplar: Data about the image, such as its resolution and the date it was taken.

questions.example: Data stored about the image rather than in it, such as its resolution, colour depth, the date it was taken and the camera used.
questions.paraphrase: Information describing the file itself — its dimensions, when it was made, what took it.
questions.feedback: Metadata is the data about the data. Without the resolution in it, nothing would know what shape the pixels go in.

questions.q: A photograph is saved at a lower resolution to make the file smaller. Explain the effect this has on the image.

markPoints.concept: there are fewer pixels in the image
accept: fewer pixels|less pixels|fewer points|smaller number of pixels|lower resolution|reduced resolution
markPoints.exemplar: There are fewer pixels in the image.

markPoints.concept: so less detail is stored and the image looks blurred or blocky
markPoints.exemplar: This means less detail is kept, so the image looks blocky.

questions.example: Lowering the resolution means there are fewer pixels, so less detail is recorded and the picture looks blurred or blocky when it is enlarged.
questions.paraphrase: The picture is made of fewer points, which means finer detail is thrown away and it appears pixelated.
questions.feedback: Fewer pixels, therefore less detail. The second mark is the consequence.
